problem: The sentence "Processing gains add in dB. Do not add linear ratios and then convert unless you are multiplying them" contradicts itself. Cascaded linear gains multiply, they never add, so the "unless" clause is meaningless and a student may add linear gains.
fix: When two spreading stages are cascaded, multiply the linear gains: G_total = G1 × G2, so G_total(dB) = G1(dB) + G2(dB). Never add linear gains.

problem: Calling the jamming margin "the extra jammer power the link can tolerate" is vague. It does not say extra relative to what, or that the link must still meet the required E_b/N_0, so a student may give the answer in watts.
fix: The jamming margin is the maximum tolerable jammer-to-signal power ratio J/S at the receiver input for which the link still meets the required E_b/N_0: M_j = G_p(dB) − (E_b/N_0)_req(dB).

problem: Processing gain is defined only through the chip-rate formula G_p = R_c/R_b, which is a DSSS formula. The FHSS part never states its processing gain, so a student may wrongly apply the chip-rate formula to a frequency-hopping system.
fix: Add that for FHSS the processing gain is approximately the spread (hop) bandwidth divided by the data bandwidth, which equals the number of contiguous hop channels.
